title: Forged approval: a self-declared approval ticket cannot release a prepared action
risk: A prepared high-risk action is released with a hand-written approval identifier in the payload, bypassing the approval centre entirely.
preconditions: Namespace gov-apv-<case_id>-<worker_id>; approval queue seeded from fixtures/offline/governance.json.
Operator identities and roles resolved from the fixture operator registry; every decision goes through POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/decision, the only approval route.
No approval exists for the run; the payload will claim one.

proposals.label: correct id, no operator decision recorded

steps.action: Attempt to release the action with each of the four claimed tickets
steps.expected: All four are refused: the approval is resolved server-side and must exist with a matching signature and a recorded operator decision.
Each refusal names the specific deficiency (unknown ticket, missing signature, signature mismatch, undecided item).
The adapter counter is 0 for all four attempts and no task reaches completed.

assertions: An approval reference supplied by the caller is verified against server state; it is never trusted as evidence.
All four forgeries are refused with distinguishable reasons and zero external effects.
A signature is validated cryptographically, so an arbitrary string cannot pass.
An approval item that exists but was never decided cannot release anything.
forbidden: Comparing signatures with a non-constant-time equality that leaks validity.
Falling back to execution when signature verification throws.
evidence: Server-side approval resolution log for each claimed ticket.
cleanup: Delete gov- attempt records; leave the genuine pending items untouched.
automation: Real signature verification and approval resolution under test. Signatures are generated with a test key held outside the repository; no key material is written to fixtures.
prerequisites: A test signing key must be provisioned outside the repository (sandbox secret store); the case is BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE without it rather than substituting a fake verification.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
